title: Apoptosis as anticancer mechanism: function and dysfunction of its modulators and targeted therapeutic strategies

grounded.evidence_quote: The tumor suppressor p53 is a transcription factor that, upon DNA damage, is activated to induce sequence-specific target genes involved in either cancer cell growth arrest or apoptosis [112].
in response to genotoxic stress, however, p53 undergoes post-translational modifications that allow the protein to escape MDM2 control, accumulate, and become active [133].
